STEP 1 - goal: fix the geometry conventions and pick a coupling position that the earlier rounds did not occupy, before writing the block.
WHAT I CHECKED: list_directory(.) -> only progress.jsonl in my workspace; read_file(tools/research/contracts/HYPERBOLIC_GEOMETRY_CONTRACT.md) -> error, not readable from here. So I use the contract conventions quoted verbatim in the round objective (ball curvature kappa=-c, c>0, R_c=1/sqrt(c), d_c(x,y)=(2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-x)(+)y||), exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||)).
REJECTED (already probed/rejected, must not restate): per-codeword curvature field (OCCURV-FIELD-RQ), stratified-curvature behaviour-marginal hyperbolic Sinkhorn (strataot-curv-rq), branching-adaptive shallow curvature from behaviour-set radial coordinates (brancurv-l1-rq), l1 geodesic-success drift, anchor-ladder, taper-innovation, dual-ramp capacity units, sign-curvature ladder, cross-graph two-segment transport.
DECISION: occupy the position "behaviour offset is a POPULARITY-ADJUSTED TRANSITION SURPLUS (not raw demand, not branching, not a curvature field), applied as a geodesic margin on LEVEL-1 only; curvature fixed and DERIVED from the measured training latent RMS (c=(rho/s)^2, rho=0.5), offset coefficient DERIVED as a fraction of the median level-1 geodesic residual so no constant is tuned". Level 2/3, residual recursion, reconstruction codebook and STE stay byte-identical to baseline. Switches: behaviour-off => m_i==1 => offset 0; geometry-off => c=0 => d -> 2||u-q||. One run, no arm trained with switches off.
OPEN: numeric safeguards (clamp of ||(-p)(+)q||), zero-residual gradient, EMA freeze/no-grad.

ANSWER (complete block, same as my final message):
IDEA: pmi-geomargin-l1-rq
TITLE: Popularity-adjusted transition-surplus geodesic margin on the level-1 Poincare assignment of an RQ-VAE Semantic ID
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE level-1 codes are learned from reconstruction geometry only, so two items that are behaviourally interchangeable as next items (same directed-transition role) can land on different level-1 codes, and a level-1 code that is the true branching point of many training transitions gets no extra pull. The generative recommender then has to spend prefix capacity on distinctions the transition graph says are irrelevant and misses distinctions it says are load-bearing.
NOVELTY: The behaviour term is a popularity-adjusted directed-transition SURPLUS (PMI-style) per level-1 codeword, not raw demand, not branching entropy, not a per-codeword curvature field, not a Sinkhorn/stratified transport, and it is not a curvature ladder. The curvature is a single FIXED value derived from the measured training latent RMS, and the offset weight is derived from a measured geodesic scale in epoch 1, so no constant is swept. Level 2, level 3, residual recursion and reconstruction codebook are byte-identical to baseline; the coupling lives only in the level-1 score.
KEY_CHANGE: Level-1 assignment score becomes the Poincare distance between the level-1 residual lifted into a derived-curvature ball and the level-1 codeword lifted into the same ball, minus a derived scalar times the log of the popularity-adjusted transition surplus of that codeword. Nothing downstream consumes the offset; the shipped codebook positions, the level-2/3 recursion, the reconstruction and the STE are unchanged.
SPECIFICATION: (1) s = RMS of the training-split latent vectors over the frozen encoder output at step 0 (per-vector L2 RMS), frozen. (2) curvature c = (rho/s)^2 with documented default rho = 0.5, so ball radius R_c = s/rho; c is fixed, never trained. (3) For a level-1 residual r: u = exp_0^c(r), q_k = exp_0^c(a_k) with a_k the unmodified baseline level-1 codebook. (4) D_k = d_c(u, q_k) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh( sqrt(c) * ||(-u)(+)q_k|| ). (5) off_k = w * log(1 + b_k), b_k the frozen mean-normalized popularity-adjusted transition surplus (see BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION). (6) k1 = argmin_k (D_k - off_k), ties to the smallest index. (7) loss = baseline reconstruction + baseline commitment, unchanged, with the straight-through estimator; the reconstruction dequantizes with a_{k1} (the baseline codebook vector), exactly as baseline, so the offset never moves the reconstruction point. (8) w = rho_off * mean_scale / max_k log(1+b_k) with rho_off = 0.10 (documented default) and mean_scale = the running mean of min_k D_k over epoch 1, frozen from epoch 2 on. (9) switches: BEHAVIOUR_OFF sets m_i = 1 for all i so b_k = 1 and off_k = w*log(2) - w*log(2) = 0 (implemented as off_k = 0 exactly, not as a subtraction); GEOMETRY_OFF sets c = 0, exp_0^0 = identity and D_k = 2*||u - q_k||, everything else identical. Only the both-on arm is trained this round.
COST: +2 to 4 percent wall clock on the same 3000-epoch, 4-card, frozen Stage-3 protocol. Per step (batch 24556/24 = 1023 items, K1 = 256 level-1 codes): one exp_0^c on 1023 vectors, one exp_0^c on the 256 codebook rows (cacheable per step), and 1023*256 artanh instead of 1023*256 Euclidean reductions inside the level-1 distance only, i.e. about 0.26 M extra transcendental ops and 0.26 M extra flops per step against an encoder/decoder forwar

d-backward on 1023 items; levels 2-3 and the decoder add nothing.
HYPOTHESIS: Items that occupy the same directed-transition role must share level-1 codes and codewords that are popular transition targets must absorb more items, so the level-2/3 prefixes see a behaviour-aligned first bit. If true, when the coupling is on the level-1 usage histogram shifts mass toward high-surplus codewords, the training-split prefix hit rate of the level-1 code of the true next item rises, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, best so far 0.0638). If the level-1 usage histogram and the prefix hit rate are indistinguishable from the Euclidean/behaviour-off behaviour, the idea is dead.
RISKS: The offset is a constant per codeword, so it can collapse several codewords into one attractor and starve the rest, which would move recall the wrong way; the popularity-adjusted surplus may be dominated by a few hub items; the level-1 change may be washed out because level 2 and 3 carry most of the prefix information; fixing rho = 0.5 may place the residuals too close to the origin for the curvature to matter; a single fixed w may be too weak or too strong and cannot be tuned under the policy; seed noise alone may exceed the gain since only one run decides it.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Popularity-adjusted directed item-transition surplus, aggregated per level-1 codeword by soft assignment weights (a training-only graph-centrality signal over observed transitions).
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the training split interactions only, build directed counts t_ij (i consumed before j in a session, consecutive pairs, self-pairs dropped). For each training item i with out-degree out_i, define its surplus mass m_i = sum_j t_ij / sqrt(out_i * in_j + eps), which damps hubs on both sides. Per epoch, using the current level-1 codes of the training latents, compute soft weights p_ik = softmax_k(-D_ik / tau) with tau = 1 (distances are already in ball units, documented default), then b_raw_k = sum_i p_ik * m_i / (sum_i p_ik + eps) over the 24556 training items of that epoch; update an EMA b_raw <- (1 - eta) * b_raw + eta * b_raw_epoch with eta = 0.1 documented default, initialized to 1; freeze with no gradient (detach and no_grad) and normalize to the codeword mean, b_k = log(1 + b_raw_k / mean_k b_raw_k). Only training items and only training transitions ever enter m_i and b_k.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: m_i and b_k are built exclusively from the training-split transition counts and from the training-split item latents; the validation and test interaction logs are never read when the table is built and the table is frozen with respect to gradients. Because the table is a per-codeword scalar (256 floats) derived only from training co-occurrence, no per-example validation or test signal can be memorized, and Stage-3 evaluation only consumes the trained codebook and encoder, exactly as in the baseline.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Poincare ball of fixed negative curvature kappa = -c with c = (rho/s)^2, R_c = 1/sqrt(c); exponential map exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)||v||) and distance d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c) * ||(-x)(+)q|| ) with the Mobius addition of the contract; the tangent-space Euclidean norm is not the Riemannian norm (||v||_{0,c} = 2||v||) and is used only inside exp_0^c.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: In the level-1 quantization step of Stage-2 training: the residual lift, the codebook lift and the level-1 assignment distance. Levels 2 and 3, the reconstruction

and the STE remain Euclidean and identical to baseline.
COUPLING PATH: A single scalar per codeword, b_k, is computed from the directed-transition graph and enters the SAME expression that contains the curved distance, so the level-1 argmin cannot be formed without both terms: removing the behaviour term sets b_k = 1 and the margin vanishes, removing the curvature sets c = 0 and the geodesic distance becomes a Euclidean one, and both cases change the same argmin.
COUPLING EQUATION: k1 = argmin_k [ d_c( exp_0^c(r), exp_0^c(a_k) ) - w * log(1 + b_k) ], with w = rho_off * mean_scale / max_k log(1 + b_k), b_k the popularity-adjusted transition surplus, mean_scale the frozen epoch-1 mean of min_k d_c.
OBSERVABLES: level-1 code usage histogram and its entropy (diagnostic, not a gate); fraction of test sequences whose true next item's level-1 code is among the top-2 codes predicted from the item's training transition neighbours (prefix behaviour predictability, diagnostic); distribution of the level-1 assignment margin D_(1) - D_(2) minus the offset difference; Stage3 test_recall@10 (the judgement).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: Same code with m_i = 1 for every item, which gives b_raw_k identical for all k, b_k = log(2) for all k, and the implementation forces off_k = 0 exactly; the level-1 assignment is then pure geodesic nearest neighbour in the derived ball. Correct in code, not trained this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: Same code with c = 0: exp_0^0 is the identity and d_0(x,y) = 2||x - y||, so the level-1 score is the Euclidean distance 2||r - a_k|| minus w * log(1 + b_k); note the derived w is recomputed against mean_scale of the Euclidean run so the switch stays scale-consistent. Correct in code, not trained this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: The full coupled run: fixed derived curvature c = (rho/s)^2 with the Poincare lift and geodesic distance, plus the frozen popularity-adjusted transition surplus offset with its derived weight w. This is the only arm trained, once, with no sweep and no seed repetition.
SPEC EQUATIONS: s = rms(latents_train); c = (rho/s)^2; R_c = 1/sqrt(c); LIFT(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)*||v|| + 1e-12) with the fallback LIFT(0) = 0; MOBIUS(x,y) = ((1 + 2c<x,y> + c||y||^2) x + (1 - c||x||^2) y) / (1 + 2c<x,y> + c^2||x||^2||y||^2); DIST(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( min(sqrt(c)*||MOBIUS(-x,y)||, 1 - 1e-6) ); per step: u = LIFT(r); q = LIFT(a); D_k = DIST(u, q_k); score_k = D_k - off_k; k1 = argmin_k score_k; r_next = r - a_{k1} (baseline, unchanged); loss unchanged; per epoch: refresh b_raw by EMA from training transitions and detach; after epoch 1 set mean_scale = running mean of min_k D_k and w = rho_off * mean_scale / max_k log(1 + b_k).
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: the level-1 residual batch r (B x d), the baseline level-1 codebook a (K1 x d), the frozen per-codeword surplus b (K1), the scalar c and the derived w. Outputs: the level-1 index k1 (B), the level-1 residual for level 2 (B x d, baseline formula), and the unchanged baseline loss; side outputs are the diagnostics (usage histogram, margin statistics, prefix hit rate).
SAFEGUARDS: clamp sqrt(c)*||MOBIUS(-x,y)|| to 1 - 1e-6 before artanh; use artanh(z) = 0.5*log((1+z)/(1-z)) in float32 with the clamp; guard every 1/sqrt(c) and division by ||v|| with an explicit c == 0 and ||v|| == 0 branch so the geometry-off switch cannot produce NaN; clamp the lifted radius to (1 - 1e-4)*R_c; detach and no_grad the surplus table and its EMA so no gradient reaches the beha

viour statistics; eps = 1e-8 in every denominator of m_i and b_raw; force off_k = 0 exactly when BEHAVIOUR_OFF; keep the reconstruction dequantization on a_{k1} so the offset cannot create a train/eval mismatch; assert determinism of the tie-break by smallest index.
END IDEA
